title: EqGINO: Equivariant Geometry-Informed Fourier Neural Operators for 3D PDEs
claim: Irregular inputs are mapped to a grid, mixed globally by symmetry-constrained spectral layers, then decoded back, preserving equivariance throughout.
layout: Top end-to-end flow left-to-right, bottom zoomed inset of spectral layer
description: A two-tier method diagram. The top row runs left to right. A dark blue 3D mesh part becomes a point cloud with a red local-aggregation region, then a blue spatial grid. It passes through dark blue EqFNO layer boxes K_1 … K_l, then a second grid, and then a point cloud with an orange decoder neighborhood. The final output is a rainbow-colored predicted field on the mesh. Headers read 'EqGNO encoder' and 'EqGNO decoder', with a legend for spatial grid (blue dots) and spectral grid (red dots). Dashed lines expand the layer into a gray inset titled 'Isotropic Spectral Convolution'. The inset shows blue grid → F → red spectral grid → multiplication by colored orbit-based weights W(k) → F^-1 → blue grid, with a skip path S, a plus node and a sigma activation. Callout labels give the math notation.
caption: Overview of EqGINO. The encoder E aggregates local geometric information from irregular inputs P and maps it to regular spatial grid. Within the Fourier layers Kl, orbit-based weights W(k) mix the Fourier-transformed feature vectors (Fv)(k) at each Fourier mode k, ensuring equivariance. The decoder D projects the updated features vL(xgrid) enriched with global context back to the point cloud to predict the physical field u (e.g., deflection, pressure). All modules preserve equivariance by construction.
abstract: Deep learning surrogates for 3D Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) often fail to generalize across geometric transformations because they depend heavily on specific coordinate systems. While equivariant networks offer a solution, they typically rely on local operations in the spatial domain, making the global receptive field, which is essential for PDE dynamics, computationally expensive. Conversely, Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) efficiently capture global interactions, yet establishing 3D equivariance within them remains impractical due to the prohibitive cost of spectral group convolutions. To bridge this gap, we introduce EqGINO, a geometrically robust framework that enforces isotropy in the spectral domain. By design, EqGINO guarantees exact equivariance to the discrete symmetries inherent to the discretized computational domain. Beyond this discrete guarantee, our structural prior enables effective generalization to arbitrary continuous orientations even with a limited number of SE(3)-transformed training samples. Consequently, our method robustly models coordinate-invariant physical laws on complex irregular 3D geometries. Our code is available at https://github.com/sung-won-kim/EqGINO
